source.title_on_document: Is ChatGPT detrimental to innovation? A field experiment among university students

supplement.where: Supporting documents with the consent-form screenshot and experimental script are mentioned on p. 9; S1 experimental script is cited on p. 11; appendix II is cited on p. 14. No direct supplement URL is supplied in the saved PDF.
supplement.holds: S1 contains the experimental script, including the consent procedure. Appendix II contains other innovation tests described as insignificant in the main text (p. 14); their definitions and numerical results cannot be checked in this PDF. The supplement is absent. The saved PDF does include the main figures and tables as image-only pages after the references, including Table 2 regression coefficients and parenthesized precision values on PDF p. 30.

paper_design_summary: Senior undergraduates in two existing courses at an Egyptian public university wrote graded essays with ChatGPT or without it; the authors describe course enrollment as the unit of randomization (pp. 7-8, Methods). One week after the assignments, the same study continued with a lab lemonade-stand game: participants chose sales parameters and advertising slogans, with within-person strategy exploration computed and slogan creativity rated by blinded external annotators (pp. 9-10). These creativity outcomes concern the period after the ChatGPT essay intervention; the paper also measures risk taking and effort, which are outside this screening scope.

studies.label: Course-level ChatGPT essay intervention with delayed laboratory innovation outcomes

assignment.what_was_assigned: The authors report course enrollment as the unit of randomization: Social Network Analysis received the ChatGPT intervention and Data Mining was the control (p. 8). These were two existing courses, not individually randomized students. The procedure used to allocate the courses by chance is not described; classification records the authors' explicit randomization claim, with this limitation flagged for audit.
assignment.quote: We used the enrollment in either of these two courses as our unit of randomization to assign participants to either the treatment or the control.
assignment.locator: p. 8, Methods, lines 169-181; p. 17, Discussion, lines 371-377
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 7, Methods, lines 154-155, calls the experiment pre-registered; p. 16, Discussion, lines 361-363, mentions a pre-registered hypothesis. No registry URL, identifier or dated protocol is provided in this PDF.

arms.name: ChatGPT essay assignments (Social Network Analysis course)
arms.description: Students in Social Network Analysis were asked to write the essay assignments using ChatGPT (p. 8, Methods). Table 1 has 50 people in this arm after the payout-information exclusion but before the subsequent outlier removals (PDF p. 29; exclusions in pp. 11-12). The final analyzed arm count is not given, so n_analyzed is null.

arms.name: No-ChatGPT essay assignments (Data Mining course)
arms.description: Students in Data Mining wrote the essay assignments with ChatGPT neither mentioned nor allowed (p. 8, Methods). Table 1 has 43 people in this arm after the payout-information exclusion but before the subsequent outlier removals (PDF p. 29; exclusions in pp. 11-12). The final analyzed arm count is not given, so n_analyzed is null.

participants.exclusions: The paper reports 94 initially recruited subjects and one exclusion for missing information during payouts (p. 11). Table 1 reports 93 people, comprising 43 control and 50 ChatGPT (PDF p. 29). Two anomalous observations were then removed using the 1.5xIQR rule (p. 12). Table 2 reports 91 participant observations in both innovation regression models (PDF p. 30). Counts at assignment, allocation of the excluded people to arms, and separate participant counts for the slogan analysis are not given. Recruitment is not relabeled as randomization.
participants.who: Senior undergraduates at an Egyptian public university, sharing a social sciences major and social science computing minor, enrolled in Social Network Analysis or Data Mining (pp. 7-8, Methods).
participants.quote: A total of 94 subjects were initially recruited for the experiment. However, one subject was discarded due to missing information during payouts.

ai_tool.how_used: Treatment students were asked to use ChatGPT to write their graded essay assignments. Researchers created accounts using foreign cell phone numbers because local access was not yet available at the time (pp. 8-9, Methods). No specific prompting protocol or model version is described. The later lab innovation task is described separately from this intervention (pp. 9-10).

task.description: Mixed writing and business-simulation task. The intervention comprised three graded essay assignments (p. 8). The follow-up required sales strategies for a hypothetical lemonade stand over seven rounds: location, color, sugar content, lemon concentration, price, and an advertising message or slogan of at most 20 words. Sugar, lemon concentration and price were chosen on scales from 0 to 10. Feedback on profits followed each round, while slogans were not part of monetary payoffs and were rated for creativity afterward (p. 10). The scored creative writing consists of the slogans; no creativity or diversity results for the intervention essays are reported.
task.duration: Essay intervention over one month during term time in April 2023 (p. 8); lab follow-up one week after all assignments were submitted (p. 9), with seven rounds in the innovation game (p. 10). No per-essay or lab-session time limit is stated.

outcomes.name: Creativity of advertising messages in the later lemonade-stand game
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Four external annotators rated advertising messages after the experiment and were unaware of the research question and experimental design (p. 10, Methods). Methods describes a 0 to 10 creativity scale, whereas Results describes a 1 to 10 innovation scale (p. 14). Results reports 265 unique messages because participants sometimes retained a message across rounds (p. 14). This is the number of rated outputs, not people. The paper does not state whether the Mann-Whitney comparison used message-level scores or scores aggregated by participant; unit is therefore null. Figure 3 provides plotted means and error bars without numeric labels or a definition of the error bars (PDF p. 25).
outcomes.delay: One week after all essay assignments were submitted (p. 9, Methods). The scored messages were produced during the subsequent lab game (p. 10).

contrasts.treatment_arm: ChatGPT essay assignments (Social Network Analysis course)
contrasts.reported: Mann Whitney U test, p-value > 0.05. No significant difference in creativity of the advertising messages. Numeric arm means, SDs, exact p-value and U statistic are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 14, Results, First: Innovative Behaviour, lines 295-302; PDF p. 25, Figure 3

outcomes.name: Aggregate exploration of sales strategies
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The paper describes the outcome as the average, subject-specific standard deviation of strategy choices for sugar content, lemon concentration and price over the lemonade-stand game (p. 13, Results; seven rounds in p. 10, Methods). It is a behavioral proxy for innovative search, coded as flexibility because variation is within each participant, not across people; it is not a count of conceptual categories. The unadjusted comparison and both regression specifications are kept together as variants of this outcome. Table 2 labels the dependent variable Exploration of sales strategies and states that results are clustered by Subject ID (PDF p. 30). The reported uncertainty does not reflect assignment at the course level. Figure 2 has no numeric labels on its estimates or definition of its error bars (PDF p. 24). The prose calls the regression difference approximately 0.6 to 0.72 standard deviation points (p. 13), but the dependent variable itself is based on within-person SDs; no between-person standardizer is specified, so this is not coded as a standardized effect size.
outcomes.delay: One week after all essay assignments were submitted (p. 9, Methods).

contrasts.reported: Mann Whitney U test, p-value = 0.037 (p. 13). Table 2: ChatGPT coefficient -0.719** (0.326) in model (1), and -0.604* (0.328) in model (2); Observations 91 in each model. Table note: Results are clustered by Subject ID; *** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1. Parenthesized regression precision values are retained as printed; the table does not explicitly label the parentheses.

company_involvement.description: No company affiliation, funding or other company involvement is reported in the saved document. Author affiliations and the acknowledgments identify academic/institutional collaborators; the use of ChatGPT alone is not coded as company involvement.

eligibility.reason: The authors explicitly describe course enrollment as the unit of randomization to ChatGPT or no ChatGPT during ordinary coursework (p. 8, Methods); this is coded as an author-reported class-level field RCT, with the unreported chance-allocation procedure flagged for audit (also p. 17, limitations). Table 2 has 91 people analyzed, exceeding 50 (PDF p. 30; exclusions pp. 11-12). Advertising slogans produced in the subsequent lab session were scored by external raters for creativity (p. 10, Methods; p. 14, Results), satisfying the output criterion independently of the strategy-exploration proxy. The scored work follows the essay intervention by one week (p. 9), so the question is after_ai. Only two courses were assigned, and Table 2 reports clustering by Subject ID rather than course; core screening inclusion does not establish that its precision is suitable for pooling.

one_line_finding: After the ChatGPT essay intervention, strategy exploration was lower (ChatGPT coefficients -0.719 (0.326) and -0.604 (0.328), 91 observations; PDF p. 30, Table 2), while rated advertising-message creativity showed no significant difference (Mann Whitney U test, p-value > 0.05; p. 14, Results).
open_questions: The local file is the April 5, 2024 bioRxiv preprint, despite its 2026 filename; how does the journal version differ? The journal version was not provided in retrieval.json and was not screened.

Were the two courses actually allocated to conditions by chance, and by what procedure? The authors call enrollment the unit of randomization (p. 8) and course registration the criterion for randomization (p. 17), but supply no sequence or mechanism. Individual students were not randomized, and Table 2 clusters by Subject ID rather than course.

Which arm contained the payout-information exclusion and which arms contained the two outliers? Table 1 gives the earlier 43/50 split (PDF p. 29), while Table 2 gives only the final total of 91 (PDF p. 30).

Can S1, appendix II and the preregistration be obtained? They are not included or directly linked in the saved PDF; appendix II holds additional innovation tests and S1 holds the experimental script (pp. 9, 11, 14). The script is also needed to verify the exact restrictions on AI access during the lab task; the main text describes a later spillover test but does not explicitly state an AI-access prohibition in that session (pp. 5, 9-10).

For slogan creativity, were the scores analyzed per message or averaged per participant, how were the four ratings combined, and which participants were included? The 265-message count does not answer these questions (p. 14). The scale is 0 to 10 in Methods (p. 10) and 1 to 10 in Results (p. 14).

For the strategy-exploration outcome, confirm the exact aggregation of the three within-person SDs, the meaning of the figure error bars, and the parenthesized regression precision values before effect-size extraction. The prose calls the aggregate an average and interprets differences in standard deviation points, without describing between-person standardization (p. 13; PDF pp. 24, 30).
notes: Read the entire markdown conversion (885 lines, including references and trailing image-page placeholders) and inspected all image-only figure/table pages of the 32-page PDF. PDF page numbers are physical, one-based page indices; the main text is numbered 1-22, Figures 1-6 occupy PDF pp. 23-28, and Tables 1-4 occupy PDF pp. 29-32. S1 and appendix II are absent. Five outcomes are recorded: rated slogan creativity, aggregate strategy exploration, and the three separately tested strategy parameters. The two regression specifications are retained within the aggregate outcome, not counted as extra outcomes. No outcome is across_people: subject-specific variation compares each participant's own strategies. Risk taking and effort are omitted because they are not creativity/diversity scores on creative output (pp. 14-16); additional unspecified innovation tests in the absent appendix cannot be enumerated (p. 14). The study is reported as pre-registered, but no outcome is explicitly designated primary in the available text, so primary is not_stated throughout. The field intervention and later lab session form one study, not separate samples. No reuse of another paper's participants is stated; adaptation of the Ederer and Manso game (p. 10) is not sample overlap. No data or code repository is given. No effect size was calculated and no plotted values were estimated. The slogan outcome's unit is deliberately null because the analysis unit is not stated; n_units=265 records the reported message corpus, not a confirmed independent-observation count. The after_ai/no-AI timing coding follows the described post-intervention lab spillover design; explicit lab access restrictions remain an open question.
